title: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Divergences in Office Documents
abstract: arXiv:2611.05806v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Office documents are now routinely uploaded to large language models (LLMs) for processing. However, an LLM does not always see what a human sees, because it typically reads the text that an extractor produces from the document's underlying Office Open XML (OOXML) files. Depending on the implementation, extractors differ in which OOXML parts they read and how they interpret them, so their output can differ from what Office applications display. For example, by slightly shifting the positions of text boxes on a slide, an adversary can swap the order in which the model reads them while the slide looks unchanged. We show that this extraction divergence is an attack surface for LLM applications.   In this work, we first measure what an adversary can exploit by analyzing the widely used extractors that LLM applications rely on. translated_title: 当文件摄取误导语言模型：测量与缓解Office文档中的分歧
translated_abstract: Office文档如今经常被上传到大型语言模型（LLM）进行处理。然而，LLM并不总是能看到人类所看到的内容，因为它通常读取的是提取器从文档底层的Office Open XML（OOXML）文件中生成的文本。由于实现方式不同，各个提取器在读取哪些OOXML部分以及如何解释这些部分上存在差异，因此其输出可能与Office应用程序所显示的内容不一致。例如，攻击者只需稍微移动幻灯片上文本框的位置，就能改变模型读取它们的顺序，而幻灯片在外观上没有任何变化。我们证明这种“提取分歧”是LLM应用程序的一个攻击面。在本工作中，我们首先通过分析LLM应用程序所依赖的广泛使用的提取器，测量攻击者能够利用的内容。通过结合静态源代码分析与动态分析，我们识别出19个提取器会读取（而用户可能无法察觉）的OOXML通道。
tldr: 该论文揭示了LLM处理Office文档时的“提取分歧”——即提取器输出与用户所见内容不一致——可被攻击者利用为攻击面，并通过静态与动态分析识别出19个可被利用的OOXML通道。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that extraction divergence—where an LLM's file extractor produces different content from what users see in Office documents—constitutes an exploitable attack surface, identifying 19 exploitable OOXML channels through combined static and dynamic analysis.
